Severity: HIGH / CVSS 7.5 (v3.1)
Summary: ## Summary The public CCG lexicon parser `nltk.ccg.lexicon.fromstring` parses caller-influenced lexicon text with two pure-Python loops whose cost is quadratic in the input width. atom:entry.atom:title: ag-psd can exhaust memory when parsing crafted PSD dimensions
atom:entry.atom:summary:
Severity: HIGH / CVSS 7.5 (v3.1)
Summary: ### Summary readPsd() commits the image/layer buffers from the declared header geometry (width x height x channels x depth, and per-layer rectangles) before validating those values against the actual data. A tiny crafted PSD declaring huge geometry forces a multi-gigabyte allocation. ### Impact On ag-psd 30.2.0, Node 24, a 52-byte PSD makes readPsd(buf) commit ~3.17 GB (measured peak RSS) in ~0.45 s before throwing a catchable RangeError ("Offset is outside the bounds of the DataView") - about 61,000,000x amplification. Because the buffer is committed before validation, the allocation OOM-kills the process before the error on essentially any host (uncatchable), and concurrent requests exhaust memory. In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
net: airoha: Do not read...
atom:entry.atom:summary:
Severity: CRITICAL / CVSS 9.8 (v3.1)
Summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: net: airoha: Do not read uninitialized fragment address in airoha_dev_xmit() The transmit loop in airoha_dev_xmit() reads fragment address and length during its final iteration, when the loop index equals skb_shinfo(skb)->nr_frags, at which point the fragment data is uninitialized. While these values are never consumed, the read itself is unsafe and may trigger a page fault. Fix this by avoiding the fragment read on the last iteration. Additionally, move the skb pointer from the first to the last used packet descriptor, so that airoha_qdma_tx_napi_poll() defers freeing the skb until the final descriptor is processed.

atom:entry.atom:title: The Node.js web service on VOS (previously Versa FlexVNF) is used for URL-based Zero Touch...
atom:entry.atom:summary:
Severity: CRITICAL / CVSS 9.1 (v3.1)
Summary: The Node.js web service on VOS (previously Versa FlexVNF) is used for URL-based Zero Touch Provisioning (ZTP) of the VOS appliance and is not required after provisioning is complete. This service generates session identifiers using UUID version 1 (UUIDv1), which is derived from the system’s date and time and its MAC address. As a result, successive identifiers differ only slightly and can be predicted. An attacker who can predict a user’s session ID could hijack that user’s session. Versa’s security hardening guide for Hubs, Branches, and Controllers recommends disabling the Node.js web service after the initial provisioning of the VOS device. This vulnerability is not exploitable on VOS devices where the Node.js web service has been disabled.

Summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: gcov: use atomic counter updates to fix concurrent access crashes GCC's GCOV instrumentation can merge global branch counters with loop induction variables as an optimization. Unlike other platforms, the Windows implementation of the update verification routine unconditionally returns success so no digital signature or trust validation is performed before staging or executing update payloads, enabling attacker‑supplied executables to be accepted and later executed by the application. Critically, Ollama for Windows performs silent automatic updates, so the malicious payload may be installed automatically without user awareness. Maintainers of this project were notified early about this vulnerability, but didn't respond with the details of vulnerability or vulnerable version range. Versions from 0.12.10 to 0.17.5 were tested and confirmed as vulnerable, other versions were not tested but might also be vulnerable.
Suggested next step: Check whether the named product and affected versions are in use; follow the original vendor's remediation guidance.

atom:entry.atom:title: bitcoinjs-lib: Undetected merkle node duplication in block root computation validates a forged transaction list
atom:entry.atom:summary:
Severity: CRITICAL
Summary: ### Summary `fastMerkleRoot` pads an odd level by hashing the last node with itself. It does not report that it did so, and `checkTxRoots` never looks for repeated transactions. A peer can therefore duplicate transactions to fill the pad and produce a block with a different transaction list but the same merkle root. The block hash and block id do not change, so the header still carries valid proof of work. In the proof of concept a real mainnet block goes from nine transactions to ten, and separately to twelve, with the same id every time, and `checkTxRoots` accepts all three. Bitcoin Core rejects this case through the `mutated` flag in `ComputeMerkleRoot` and the `bad-txns-duplicate` reason in `CheckBlock`.
